Lowest = $50. keep_max = 50 / 1.22 = 40.98, round down to nearest $5 = $40 (all-in $48.80). Flip: likely resale about $65 (middle of verified sales); less about 20% seller commission at a Tasmanian room ($13) and $0 postage (pickup furniture) = $52; 52 / 2.44 = 21.3, round down = $20. Inbound freight $0. Unverified index figures ($15-$225) were not used for bids.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification from five good photos and no maker's mark to read; only three SOLD prices verified on opened pages, and two of those came with loose backs. Most Invaluable prices are hidden behind log-in, so unverified. Timber (cedar v mahogany) not confirmed.

These have backs, different columns or legs, so they are not the same item, and their prices are unverified. Two consecutive-offering pairs were merged into single entries. Invaluable lot pages fetched by curl returned HTTP 202 (bot challenge) after the first; not worked around.
lots.key_photo_findings: Five photos: front, three-quarter, corbel close-up, doors and drawer open, top with drawer open. Top shows two small holes or plugs at the back corners where a superstructure was fixed; no back present. Door panels flame figured, reddish timber consistent with cedar but could be mahogany. Drawer bottom pale secondary timber. One fixed shelf; lock keep on right door, no key seen. Corbel carving intact in close-up (researcher's 'cracked corbel' not clearly visible to me). No maker's mark or label.
lots.condition: Sound looking. Polish faded and scuffed, especially the top and plinth; minor knocks; screw holes in top from missing back; lock and key not confirmed.
lots.question_for_armitage: What are the dimensions, is the timber cedar or mahogany, is the back or superstructure with it anywhere, does the drawer run freely, and is there a key for the door lock?
